newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada union settles key issue with Chrysler.
newsitem.headline: Canada union settles key issue with Chrysler.

text.p: Canadian Auto Workers President Buzz Hargrove said late on Monday that the union had tentatively settled the key outsourcing issue that had held up labour talks with Chrysler Corp's Canadian unit.
"I think it's fair to say we have broken the log jam on the key issue of outsourcing," he told reporters. Hargrove said the agreement met the unions concerns on outsourcing decisions.
"This meets our concerns about work ownership, about limiting the company's ability to outsource our jobs simply because they can make more money," Hargrove said.
He said the late breakthrough will hold providing the final contractual language reflects the union's concerns about job security due to contracting out.
"If the language comes down the way we want we can't lose members or numbers because of outsourcing decisions," he said.
He suggested the deal-making agreement occurred in the wake of reports Ford Motor Co had reached a tentative labour pact with the United Auto Workers union in the U.S.

Hargrove said the new language on outsourcing will establish a pattern for the union to foist on Ford of Canada and the Canadian subsidiary of General Motors Corp (GM) in the next two rounds of negotiations.
"We have established a pattern that has to be met by Ford and GM," he said.
Despite optimism that a complete labour contract could be sewn up before the strike deadline on Tuesday at 2359 EDT (0359 GMT Wednesday), Hargrove cautioned there may not be enough time.
"There is no guarantee that we can get this done in time to avoid some loss in production," he said.
Hargrove said he would not extend the strike deadline to cover all the issues.
"We will have a settlement tonight (Tuesday) on all of our issues or there will be a strike," he said. "We are not moving our deadline."
Talks on an economic package, work time, health and safety issues resumed after Hargrove met with the heads of the union's committees to tell them of the outsourcing agreement.
Outsourcing is the sale of plants or transfer of work to outside contractors whose employees are not generally members of the auto unions.

The Canadian Auto Workers (CAW) union is the largest private sector union in Canada with over 200,000 members. It represents about 53,000 auto workers at the three North American automakers. Chrysler employs 12,600 members in Canada, Ford employs 11,690 and General Motors 28,510.
General Motors of Canada Ltd has said it plans to sell two plants in Canada and outsource more than 5,000 jobs.
The CAW has said it will seek to reverse those plans when it meets with GM over its labor agreements.
